alt: Bars to scale: Paper 1 Question 2 (8 marks, language), Paper 1 Question 3 (8 marks, structure), Paper 1 Question 4 (20 marks, evaluation) and Paper 2 Question 3 (12 marks, language). AO2 covers analysing language and structure; AO4 takes the step to judging.
caption: Four questions test the writer’s choices; the 20-mark evaluation is the largest.

alt: Four bands from smallest to largest unit: vocabulary (single words), grammar (how words are arranged), form (the kind of text and its conventions) and structure (the whole text as a sequence), each with the features to look for.
caption: Words, arrangement, kind of text, whole sequence: four places to look for choices.

alt: A table pairs grammar choices with effects: a simple sentence after complex ones emphasises an idea; long sentences mimic breathlessness; questions and commands change the reader’s role; tense, pronouns, modal verbs, the passive voice and word order each shift meaning or emphasis.
caption: Grammar creates effects just as vocabulary does.

alt: A text drawn as a column of paragraphs, with labels from top to bottom: opening, shifts in focus, time, repetition and patterning (a dashed arrow loops from the end back to the start), paragraphing (a one-line paragraph) and ending.
caption: Structure is the order and shape of the whole text, from opening to ending.

alt: Three rising steps. “The writer uses a verb” is accurate but inert. “The verb ‘clawed’ gives the wind the violence of an animal” explains an effect. Evaluation judges why the choice is right at this moment or how it shapes the whole passage, with phrases such as “particularly effective because”.
caption: A term earns credit only when it leads to an effect, and then to a judgement.

alt: The opening of the Ellis passage with two phrases highlighted. The minor sentence “Too quiet” turns a neutral observation into a warning. The personified refrigerator humming “its one low note” makes the absence of human sound audible. The paragraph ends by evaluating the impact: the reader senses something is wrong before Ellis admits it.
caption: Accurate term, precise effect, then a judgement of impact.

alt: Four bands whose widths show the focus: the doorway, then outward to sounds below and above, then narrowing to the empty table, then a final separate paragraph that withholds “she had gone” until the last clause.
caption: The focus widens, narrows to one detail, then ends on a withheld certainty.
